Subject: Question on min spend and burst handling

Hi Ro han,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look promising. Before we move to a procurement review, I need to clarify a couple of commercial items so I can model this for budgeting:

- Minimum monthly spend: what is the smallest committed monthly spend you will accept for a 12-month term?
- On-demand over commit (overage) rate: if we exceed committed tokens in a given month, how are those charged? Is it a fixed multiplier over hosted list price or a separate per-token rate?
- Emergency / burst handling: if we spike for a few hours (e.g., product launch), do you have a burst buffer or short-term capacity? How is that billed versus on-demand?

Also, can you share a short term sheet and a simple usage estimate template (tokens by route) so procurement can run numbers? We can loop procurement (procurement@acmeai.com) once I have the skeleton.

Appreciate the speedy reply — we are aiming to start a pilot in May if numbers make sense.

Best,
Claire

From: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai
To: Claire Dawson <claire@acmeai.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on min spend and burst handling

Claire — thanks for the thoughtful questions. Summarizing our standard approach and an initial proposal so procurement has something concrete to review. I attached a short term sheet and the usage estimate template you asked for.

Summary (proposal):
- Minimum monthly commit: $25,000 USD (12-month term) — this secures baseline capacity and preferred burst pricing.
- On-demand overage: billed at 1.8x hosted per-token published rate (i.e., 80% premium over on-demand list) for any usage above committed tokens in a calendar month.
- Emergency burst buffer: customers get a 10% burst buffer (by token volume) above the commit that can be consumed within the month and billed at the same overage rate; for short, sub-24-hour spikes we offer best-effort capacity and will not throttle if capacity is available.
- True-up: monthly true-up against committed tokens (invoice adjusts for over/under usage). Quarterly review for any sustained overage patterns.

If you need lower friction for an initial pilot, we can do a 3-month ramp option: reduce the committed floor to $15k for the first 3 months with the same overage multiplier and a required 12-month signed term (remainder invoiced pro-rata).

Files attached: Redwood_TermSheet_v2.pdf, acme_usage_estimates_Q2.xlsx

Let me know if you and procurement want the term sheet as a tracked DocuSign so legal can start reviewing. Happy to hop on a call tomorrow with Marissa to walk through the true-up math.

Thanks,
Ro han Mehta
Head of Sales — Hosted Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Dawson <claire@acmeai.com>

Subject: Re: Question on min spend and burst handling

Ro han — thanks, that helps a lot. A few follow ups from procurement and product:

1) $25k/min is a little higher than we expected for the pilot. Can you do $12k–15k for the first quarter and then reassess? We can commit to the 12-month term but need a more gradual ramp.
2) The 1.8x overage multiplier is reasonable, but procurement asked whether you can provide a stepped overage: 1.5x for the first 90 days post-go-live (as we stabilize), then 1.8x thereafter.
3) For burst events: if we have a controlled launch window, would you consider a one-time emergency burst allotment of additional tokens (e.g., 25% of commit) billed at on-demand list price (no multiplier) if we provide 7 days notice? That would help our business case.

If you can mark these concessions on the term sheet, procurement will escalate to legal. If not, let us know which items are firm and which are negotiable.

—Claire

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme negotiation notes (do not forward)

Quick internal note before we send a redline to Acme: procurement is asking for three concessions. I recommend we accept a controlled ramp and a limited promotional overage for onboarding with guardrails. Proposed internal concession package to propose back (keeps economics predictable but helps close pilot):

- Ramp floor: $15,000/month for months 1–3; standard $25,000 effective month 4 for remainder of 12-month term. (This gives Acme runway and gets us to scale.)
- Promotional overage multiplier: 1.5x for the first 90 days from pilot start (not calendar quarter), then 1.8x thereafter.
- Emergency burst: allow one scheduled emergency burst up to 25% of commit if Acme provides at least 72 hours notice; this burst is billed at a reduced overage of 1.0x (hosted list price) for up to 48 hours. Any unscheduled or >48h bursts billed at 1.8x.

Rationale: the 72-hour scheduling requirement protects capacity planning; limited duration prevents ongoing free usage. We should require a short addendum to the term sheet clarifying ramp dates and true-up mechanics.

If Ben and Ro han agree, I can update the term sheet and send to Claire with a clean summary.

—Marissa

From: Claire Dawson <claire@acmeai.com>

Ro han / Marissa — thanks for the quick internal discussion and the updated proposal. Procurement reviewed the concession package and Acme can accept with two small edits:

1) Ramp floor: Acme agrees to $15k/month for months 1–3. On month 4 we transition to $20k/month for months 4–6, then $25k/month months 7–12 (this staggered step-up smooths our cashflow).
2) Emergency burst: the 72-hour scheduling requirement is fine, but for one "short notice" launch (<24 hours) per year we request the 25% burst at 1.0x as a one-time courtesy.

If you can send the term sheet with those two edits and a DocuSign link for signature, we can get legal to finish review today. I'll route the final to procurement@acmeai.com.

Appreciate the flexibility — excited to get the pilot started.

Best,
